Celiac Disease
Deﬁ nition Celiac disease (CD) is a complex disease whose 
etiology originates from genetic, environmental, and autoim-
mune factors triggered by the body’s abnormal reaction to
gluten.71 In this disease, exposure to the gliadin component 
of gluten results in an inﬂ ammatory response damaging the 
intestinal mucosa.
Epidemiology Epidemiological studies indicate CD is
much more common than previously thought, at approximately 
1% worldwide.72, 73 In 2003, the prevalence of CD in the United 
States was estimated to be 1:22 in ﬁ rst-degree relatives, 1:39 
in second-degree relatives, and 1:56 in symptomatic patients. 
Overall, prevalence of CD in not-at-risk groups was 1:133.74
More recently, CD was diagnosed in 30 out of a group of 
976 at-risk patients (see “Etiology”).73 Other countries, includ-
